Leverage and Capital Structure: DOL, DFL, DCL and Theories

Leverage means using fixed costs to magnify results. Fixed operating costs magnify the effect of sales on profit, and fixed interest magnifies the effect of profit on earnings per share. This guide measures both.

2 min readFor MBA, BBA and BBMUpdated 2 November 2026

A worked example

Sales ₹10,00,000; variable costs ₹4,00,000; fixed costs ₹2,00,000; interest ₹1,00,000.

Line₹
Sales10,00,000
Variable costs(4,00,000)
Contribution6,00,000
Fixed costs(2,00,000)
EBIT4,00,000
Interest(1,00,000)
EBT3,00,000

The three leverages

MeasureFormulaResultMeaning
Operating leverage (DOL)Contribution ÷ EBIT1.5A 10% rise in sales lifts EBIT by 15%
Financial leverage (DFL)EBIT ÷ EBT1.33A 10% rise in EBIT lifts EPS by 13.3%
Combined leverage (DCL)DOL × DFL = contribution ÷ EBT2A 10% rise in sales lifts EPS by 20%

It works in both directions. A 10% fall in sales would cut EPS by 20% in this example. A company with high fixed operating costs, such as an airline, should usually be careful about adding heavy debt on top.

Break-even point

Break-even sales in units = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit. With fixed costs of ₹2,00,000, a price of ₹100 and variable cost of ₹40: 2,00,000 ÷ 60 = 3,334 units (rounded up).

Capital structure theories

TheoryMain idea
Net income approachMore debt lowers WACC and raises firm value
Net operating income approachCapital structure does not change firm value
Traditional approachAn optimal mix exists: moderate debt lowers WACC, and too much raises it
Modigliani-Miller (no taxes)In perfect markets, capital structure does not matter
Modigliani-Miller (with taxes)The interest tax shield makes debt add value
Trade-off theoryBalances the tax benefit of debt against the costs of distress
Pecking order theoryFirms prefer retained profit first, then debt, and equity last

What decides capital structure in practice

  • Stability of cash flows: steady businesses can carry more debt.
  • Asset type: tangible assets support secured borrowing.
  • Tax rate: higher rates make interest deductions more valuable.
  • Control: issuing shares dilutes promoters, and debt does not.
  • Market conditions and lender covenants.

Exam and interview questions

What is the difference between operating and financial leverage?

Operating leverage comes from fixed operating costs and affects EBIT. Financial leverage comes from fixed finance costs and affects EPS.

Is a high DOL good or bad?

Neither on its own. It raises profit quickly in good times and cuts it quickly in bad times, so it suits firms with stable, growing sales.

What does Modigliani-Miller say?

Without taxes and in perfect markets, firm value does not depend on how it is financed. With corporate taxes, debt adds value through the tax shield.
